properties.state: {"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"The governance mode is chosen, visible and changeable — it is the one asserted default that is actually acted upon","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Project.mode decides whether the design or the implementation is the source of truth, and reflow2 applies it by default, never asks for it, and provides no way to change it. THE MEASURED STATE, 2026-07-28. genesis.rs takes mode OPTIONALLY — \"if let Some(mode) = opts.mode\" — and its own comment states the consequence: \"Scaffold the Project (schema applies mode=flexible, status=active when unset)\". project_mode_of falls back to \"flexible\" again on read. The string \"mode\" does not appear anywhere in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs, so there is no set_project_mode and no setter of any kind on the served surface; after genesis it is reachable only through the create_node escape hatch — the same shape as the KPP objective finding and Requirement.concern. And reflow2's OWN Project carries mode = flexible, which nobody chose. WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE TEN PROPERTIES IN THE ORIGINAL SWEEP, and the difference is the whole point. Those defaults are asserted AND UNREAD — Requirement.concern sitting at core on 67 of 67 is inert, carrying no information and driving nothing. This one is asserted AND ACTED UPON: heal.rs:431 reads it, and in rigid mode HEAL only proposes and never auto-applies. So req:defaults-do-not-assert has, in this property, its first instance where the invented value changes what the system DOES. flexible is not a neutral setting either. In the vocabulary reflow2 inherited it means the architecture is NOT the source of truth, the implementation drives the architecture, and the response to drift is to update the design to match the build. That is a governance decision. reflow2 — a project whose thesis is that the design is the memory — is currently running in the mode that says the implementation drives the design, not because anyone decided so but because opts.mode was None. THE PRIOR ART IS A FAILURE, NOT A MODEL, and it corroborates rather than instructs. reflow defined development_mode in workflow_master.json with seven behavioural commitments per mode (architecture_source_of_truth, implementation_drives_architecture, drift_response, new_functionality_policy, change_request_required, auto_update_architecture_on_resync, plus the discovered-items routing), REQUIRED it as the P0-to-P1 transition prerequisite (\"fields_must_be_set: development_mode.mode\"), READ it in resync_protocol.json to choose between updating the architecture and realigning the implementation, and TESTED for it in 97-GAN-inspired-test.json — and NO WORKFLOW STEP ANYWHERE SETS IT. Not 00a, not 00b, not the 01 through 04 series. Its own META-04H check HA-005, \"Transition Prerequisites Satisfiability\", exists to catch exactly that and did not. So both systems arrive at the same place by different routes: a governance mode that everything consults and nothing establishes. THREE THINGS THIS REQUIRES, and they are separable. (1) The value is CHOSEN — genesis asks, or the mode reads as unspecified until someone says, per the rule ver:interface-spec already sets for Interface.medium: a default may record absence, never a choice. (2) The value is CHANGEABLE — a project's governance legitimately moves as it matures, exploratory to controlled, and today it cannot; brainmaker reported this from the field, half-right, since the sharper fact is that genesis does not set it at all, it defaults it. (3) The value is VISIBLE — a mode that silently changes HEAL's behaviour should be readable in the reports that say where the design stands. What rigid should MEAN beyond heal.rs:431 stays open and parked separately; this requirement is the prior question, because rigid cannot mean anything useful while the mode is unchoosable and unchangeable. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing 00a-basic_setup.json. Anthony's word: capture it.","status":"proposed"}
